name: Claris FileMaker
tagline: Low-code database app builder for Mac, Windows, iPad and web, owned by Apple's Claris.
description: FileMaker is a low-code platform where the database, forms, scripts and permissions live in one file that FileMaker Pro designs, FileMaker Server hosts, and FileMaker Go (iPad/iPhone) or WebDirect (browser) run. It is how many small businesses, schools and departments built their own CRM, inventory and job-tracking apps without a development team. Claris, an Apple subsidiary, jumped the version number to 26 with FileMaker 2026 (June 2026), adding a Standby Server, remote backups and more AI script steps on top of earlier semantic-search features. It is great for fast internal apps; it is not a general-purpose database for large or public-facing systems.

pricing.notes: Annual per-user licensing for Pro, Server and Cloud; free 45-day trial.

scale.notes: Comfortable for departmental data and tens to low hundreds of concurrent users; Standby Server adds failover.

strengths: Non-developers can build working database apps with forms, scripts and permissions in days
Same solution runs on macOS, Windows, iPad/iPhone and in the browser
Granular privilege sets and encryption at rest built in
Data API and OData let other systems read and write FileMaker data
Built-in AI script steps and semantic find for embeddings-based search
weaknesses: Scales poorly beyond departmental data volumes and concurrency
Proprietary file format and scripting create lock-in
Per-user subscription costs add up for large user bases
Weak fit for public internet-facing applications
useCases: Small-business CRM, inventory and job tracking
Departmental apps in schools, labs and nonprofits
Replacing spreadsheets with a shared, permissioned app
notIdealFor: Teams that want code-first, Git-based development
